analysis.session_summary: The full trading day was dominated by broad USD weakness: DXY fell 0.334% and USD ranked last at -0.299%. AUD led at +0.338%, supported by risk appetite, while NZD dropped 0.457% on its employment miss before recovering most of the loss. ISM services missed but produced an inverted USD bid, signaling crowded short-dollar positioning. Political headlines from US midterms drove most of the tape.

themes.theme: Broad USD weakness on midterm political headlines
themes.evidence: DXY/USD closed -0.334%; USD currency strength -0.299%; EUR/USD +40.7 pips; AUD/USD +44.5 pips.

themes.theme: NZD employment miss initially pressured the kiwi
themes.evidence: Employment Change q/q actual -0.1% vs forecast 0.4%; NZD own impulse -0.457%; AUD/NZD closed +0.421%.

themes.theme: Inverted ISM reaction points to short-dollar positioning
themes.evidence: ISM Services PMI actual 54.5 vs forecast 54.8; USD own impulse +0.047%; EUR/USD reaction -0.042%.

currency_drivers.USD: ISM miss produced inverted USD bid, but broader political flows kept the dollar weakest.
currency_drivers.EUR: Own CPI matched forecast and was muted; EUR moved with USD weakness rather than on its own.
currency_drivers.JPY: No own catalyst; early strength faded and left a small daily loss.
currency_drivers.GBP: No own catalyst; held firm in tight range ahead of BOE.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own catalyst; strengthening reflected broad risk appetite and high-beta outperformance.
currency_drivers.CAD: No own catalyst; held a tight range with no independent directional impulse.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own catalyst; initial safe-haven bid faded, leaving only a partial gain.
currency_drivers.NZD: Own employment miss (-0.1% vs 0.4%) drove initial weakness, but selling was rejected and mostly recovered.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: The pair whipsawed through five legs: a no-catalyst drift lower, a 75.5-pip up leg helped by Japan Monetary Base, a midterm-driven dip, a 46.2-pip rally, then an ISM-led decline.

polarity_reads.read: Normal polarity: the miss sent NZD lower by 0.457%, indicating the market was not positioned for a weak print.
Inverted: USD strengthened 0.047% on a miss, implying traders were short dollars and used the dip to buy.

polarity_reads.event: Core CPI Flash Estimate y/y +1 more
polarity_reads.read: Muted: basket moved -0.032% inside noise, offering no positioning signal.

scenarios.name: USD weakness extends on political gridlock
scenarios.thesis: Midterm headlines keep the dollar offered; high-beta currencies extend gains.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD already rose 40.7 pips on USD weakness; further dollar slide extends this.
AUD led at +0.338% and closed at its best; risk-on extension favors AUD/USD.
USD/JPY fell 21.2 pips; continued USD weakness and yen haven bid add downside.

scenarios.name: Consolidation before BOE and US data
scenarios.thesis: The dollar's large move pauses; ranges dominate as the BOE and US claims approach.
triggers: BOE delivers expected 4.00% hike with no hawkish surprise

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD traded inside an 88.4-pip range; a consolidation day stays within it.
GBP/USD's 95.7-pip range gives room for a quiet pre-BOE session.
USD/JPY holds within its 136.1-pip range as yen drivers fade.

scenarios.name: BOE hawkish repricing
scenarios.thesis: BOE surprises hawkishly or Bailey pushes back on cuts, lifting sterling.
triggers: MPC vote split more hawkish than 7-0-2 forecast
Bailey signals no rush to ease
scenarios.invalidation: Bailey emphasizes downside growth risks and a dovish tone

pair_paths.rationale: GBP/USD gained 51.7 pips; hawkish BOE extends the move within its 95.7-pip range.
EUR/GBP's 26.6-pip range offers room for a drop if GBP outperforms.

risks.why_it_matters: DXY fell 0.334% on midterm news; a reversal would hit risk FX.
GBP held firm with +0.086% strength ahead of 4.00% rate; any surprise can move GBP sharply.
USD bid on ISM miss was only 0.047%; if positioning shifts, dollar may weaken further.
NZD impulse was -0.457% but recovered; further soft NZ data could renew selling.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: BOE rate decision at 13:00 with forecast 4.00% and MPC votes, plus Bailey and SNB Schlegel, then US jobless claims and BOC Macklem can refocus the market.
